Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: Design 3 Celtic poker court, first King of Spades review master. Create ONE complete flat card image, portrait 5:7 aspect ratio, preferably 1060 x 1484. No mockup, no surroundings.
Input image 1 is ONLY a composition reference from Design 1: keep the readable two-ended poker court hierarchy, relatively small head with crown clearance, broad sleeves, opposing K/spade corner indices, straight rectangular ornament frame and central join. Completely replace its Morris floral vocabulary and Renaissance clothes with a distinct traditional Celtic-inspired aesthetic.
Style: lavish but disciplined hand-painted Insular manuscript illumination, confident dark ink outlines, flat richly pigmented textile shapes, fine warm bronze detailing, gently modeled human faces. A conscious artistic synthesis of La Tene metalwork and early medieval Irish/Insular ornament, NOT fantasy Viking design.
Frame: ivory outer paper edge, bronze outlined rectangular band of clearly woven over-under interlace, small alternating red enamel and blue accents, trumpet spirals and triskele roundels. Interior midnight woad-blue field of curvilinear spiral ornament surrounding a generous shaped creamy vellum reserve behind the portraits. Dense geometric decoration, not flowers or acanthus. Keep background quieter than the face.
Figure: fictional mature Celtic sovereign, long chestnut hair and short dignified beard, both eyes visible, slight turn toward viewer RIGHT. Modest low bronze circlet with red-glass studs and spiral engraving, not tall fleur-de-lis crown. Rectangular madder-red wool mantle fastened at shoulder with a beautifully detailed round penannular-style brooch over warm weld-yellow linen tunic, restrained geometric embroidered borders, bronze torc. Broad mantle folds and sleeves fill central field. Holds upright straight iron sword on viewer RIGHT with simple short curved bronze guard, short plain grip, rounded pommel; blade tip fully inside inner frame. Other hand at chest. No plate armor, plaid kilt, horned helmet, runes, Norse dragon heads, cross, shamrocks, modern Celtic lettering.
Double-ended composition: same character repeated upside down in lower half, elegantly joined by diagonal cloth band crossing a CENTRAL small bronze roundel with double spiral design that is visually half-turn compatible. No flower jewel. Aim for clean 180-degree repetition, no visible dividing line. Both faces, hands and weapons readable.
Exact text: only large legible black serif "K" over plain black spade silhouette in upper-left ivory rounded index panel; identical panel rotated 180 degrees at lower-right. No other letters, no caption, no pseudo-Irish. All artwork inside whole card canvas, ivory outside edge at all four sides.
